title: Best DrChrono Alternative for Cash-Pay Practices (2026)
summary: Looking for a DrChrono alternative for a cash-pay clinic? See why primary care, wellness and aesthetic practices switch, and what to check first.
body_markdown:
## What Is DrChrono and Who Is It Built For?


DrChrono, owned by EverHealth, is a cloud EHR and practice management platform aimed at independent practices.[Its own site](https://www.drchrono.com/) lists scheduling, documentation, medical billing with a proprietary clearinghouse, telehealth, a patient portal and mobile apps for Apple devices, and names family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, counseling and psychiatry among its specialties.


That description fits a practice that bills insurance. The pricing page lists Foundation, Growth and Premium plans, per-claim and per-statement fees, and an integrated payments program. It is a sensible product for that job. A practice that sells botulinum toxin, testosterone programs and monthly weight loss memberships for cash is doing a different job, and the gaps show up in the same few places.


## Why Cash-Pay Practices Look for a DrChrono Alternative


Cash-pay practices leave DrChrono because the daily workflow stops matching the product, not because the software fails. These are the situations operators described to us.


### Notes that have to start from a template


One physician told us he cannot open a note and simply type. Everything has to go through a template. Templates save time for repeat injectables, but a primary care visit or an unusual consult needs a blank page. Ask any vendor to open a free-text note in the demo, then ask whether the template fields can still be added to it.


### Lab orders on paper


The same physician was printing lab orders and handing them to patients. For a practice running hormone replacement or weight loss, labs are the visit rhythm, so electronic ordering and results that land in the chart are not optional. DrChrono lists Quest and LabCorp integration on every plan and an extended lab integration for more than 40,000 labs and imaging services as a[$30 per provider per month add-on](https://www.drchrono.com/pricing/) . Confirm with your own quote what ordering looks like for the labs you use. Our guide to[med spa EMR lab integration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-lab-integration) lists what to test.


### Intake that never reaches the chart


New patients write down their medications and allergies, and someone retypes them. The goal is simple: what the patient enters on the iPad should populate their profile, and consent forms signed on the same tablet should upload to the record on their own. If a vendor needs a person to move data from a form into the chart, you have not removed the paperwork.


### Texting, email and the phone line


The practice owner wanted to text patients, send a monthly specials newsletter and stop paying a separate service for phones. DrChrono lists monthly text and phone reminder allowances by plan, with overage charges per message and per call on its pricing page. Reminders are only part of the job for a cash-pay clinic, which also needs re-engagement campaigns and a way to answer calls at ten at night. Our comparison of[AI receptionist and telephony](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-ai-receptionist-telephony-difference) explains the difference.


### Tracking refill calls with fake appointments


This one is small and telling. The practice made up appointments to record that a patient called about a refill, because the system had no other place to put it. A refill request needs a date, a status, a payment and a record that it was done. See[HRT refill workflow errors](https://decodahealth.com/blog/hrt-refill-workflow-errors) for how clinics handle it without invented visits.


## How We Compared These DrChrono Alternatives


We scored options on the problems above instead of a feature count. Does it chart in templates and in free text? Can you order labs electronically from the chart? Does intake fill the patient profile? Are texting, email and phones part of the platform? How are memberships and packages handled? And who migrates the data, and how long does it take? Vendor facts below come from each company's own site, and where a vendor does not publish a detail the table says "Not published".

**Treatment plans.** Practices that hand patients a written plan after each visit usually end up with one plan template per visit type. A hormone follow-up and a Botox visit do not share the same headings, and pulling note fields into a plan depends on the field names matching. ## When Staying on DrChrono Makes Sense


A practice that bills insurance for most of its visits, files claims every day and relies on a clearinghouse should not switch to chase a feature list. DrChrono's billing tools, eligibility checks and claim management are the reason such practices choose it, and a cash-pay platform will not replace them. Likewise, a practice whose only complaint is a renewal price is better off negotiating the renewal than starting a migration.


The practices that should move are the ones where cash services have become the business: injectables, hormones, weight loss, IV and memberships. If you are weighing options at that stage, our guide to[the best EMR for longevity clinics](https://decodahealth.com/blog/top-emr-longevity-clinics) and the comparison of[functional medicine EMRs](https://decodahealth.com/blog/functional-medicine-emr-comparison) cover the wider field.

## How to Test Any DrChrono Alternative in a Demo


The demo will look good whichever vendor runs it, so give them your worst workflows. Ask them to do each of these live:


- **Write a blank note.** Then add a template section to it.
- **Order a lab panel.** Show where the result lands and how a trend looks over two draws.
- **Run a new patient through intake.** Check whether the medication list reaches the profile without retyping.
- **Log a refill request.** It should have a status and a payment, not a pretend appointment.
- **Port your number.** Ask what happens to desk phones and to staff who answer from home.
- **Quote the whole bill.** Include texting, labs, e-prescribing and phones. Our[clinic software cost breakdown](https://decodahealth.com/blog/clinic-software-cost-breakdown) shows how to compare quotes built differently.
- **Show your accounting path.** If an office manager enters transactions into QuickBooks by hand, ask how that step disappears.


One more habit from past migrations: a physician who had already moved EMRs twice told us she lost data both times and wants this to be the last move. Ask what a failed record looks like and who fixes it. Operators who plan for that question tend to have a better go-live. The same advice appears in our[PatientNow alternative](https://decodahealth.com/blog/patientnow-alternative) and[Boulevard alternatives](https://decodahealth.com/blog/boulevard-software-alternatives) guides.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing a DrChrono Alternative


If most of your revenue still comes from insurance claims, keep DrChrono and fix the specific complaint. If the clinic has become a cash-pay business with injectables, hormones and memberships, the mismatch will keep growing, and a platform that handles charting, labs, intake, payments and phones together removes the stitched-together stack. ## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the best DrChrono alternative for a cash-pay practice?


The best fit depends on how the practice earns revenue. DrChrono is built around insurance billing, so a practice that is mostly cash-pay, with injectables, hormone therapy, weight loss and memberships, should look at a platform built for elective care. Decoda Health combines scheduling, free-form and templated charting, lab ordering, payments and phones in one system.


Why do practices leave DrChrono?


Public reviews on Capterra and G2 mention support quality, price increases and contract terms, and operators we speak with add a fit problem. A practice that drifts from insurance visits toward cash-pay services ends up with tools for claims it does not file, and gaps for memberships, packages and marketing. Individual experiences vary, so check your own agreement.


Can I move from DrChrono without losing my charts and patient records?


You should be able to, but ask each vendor in writing what transfers and who does the work. Demographics and visit notes usually move easily, while prepaid packages, membership balances and uploaded documents are the items most often dropped. Decoda Health runs the migration itself and finishes it in 3-4 weeks, guaranteed.


Does DrChrono charge extra for texting and lab access?


DrChrono lists monthly text and phone reminder allowances by plan, with per-message overage fees, and lists extended lab integration as a paid add-on. Check the current pricing page and your quote, since the totals depend on volume. Whatever platform you choose, ask for a full quote that includes the texting, labs and phone features you actually use.


Can I keep my office phone number if I change EHR systems?


Usually yes, because phone numbers can be ported to a new provider. The practical question is what happens to the desk phones and the people answering from home. Decoda Health ports the existing business number during onboarding, and staff can answer from a softphone in a browser, so the number patients already call stays the same.


Is DrChrono a good EHR for a med spa or wellness clinic?


DrChrono's own site describes it for independent practices in family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, therapy and similar insurance-billed specialties. Many wellness clinics use it successfully for charting. The friction tends to appear around memberships, packages, retail and marketing, which are core to a cash-pay clinic and are not what the product is organized around.
